A1.justification: Both complete, readable 113-page PDFs describe the same PRAXIS research. Text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices B.8 and D report original PRAXIS experiments measuring runtime, memory, recall, optimal-tree recovery and ablation outcomes.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendices B.8 and D retain original empirical results, including runtime and memory comparisons, recall estimates and caching/proxy analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 retain the same proxy-guided pruning, sibling-budget refinement and modified LicketySPLIT procedure. Appendix B implementation components and algorithm variants are unchanged.

E1.justification: Table 8 and Appendix D retain the same datasets, binarizations and evaluation scenarios. The Churn citation changes, but its prediction task, 5,000 samples and 81/472-feature representations remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain TreeFARMS, SORTeD, RESPLIT and bootstrapped LicketySPLIT. The GOSDT and STreeD comparisons in Appendix D.4 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendices C–D retain the same preprocessing, depth and regularization settings, Rashomon budgets, evaluation procedures and resource limits, including the standard 90-hour and 200-GB limits.

E4.justification: The caching ablation, missing-tree analysis, alternative-proxy evaluations, leaf-prediction comparisons, depth studies and early-stopping analysis are retained without changes in Appendices B.8 and D.

E5.justification: Tables 2 and 32 still report means and standard deviations over five bootstraps; Table 12 still reports ten bootstraps. Run-count disclosures and uncertainty reporting are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted findings and result interpretations remain unchanged throughout. For example, Table 1 reports the same PRAXIS Churn runtime of 34.84 seconds and peak memory of 279.41 MB in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, runtime and memory bounds, recovery conditions, and proofs in Section 3 and Appendices A–B are unchanged. Equation movement results from text reflow.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims of efficient Rashomon-set approximation, near-perfect recall and orders-of-magnitude runtime and memory savings.

C2.justification: Discussions of possible missed trees, conditional recovery guarantees, fingerprint collisions and proxy-dependent runtime/memory tradeoffs remain unchanged, including their appendix qualifications.

D1.justification: Implementation, preprocessing, hardware and experimental details are unchanged. The additional first-page code footnote repeats the repository address already present in the abstract, adding no new access information.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the research positioning are unchanged. The Churn source retains the book title Discovering Knowledge in Data but changes author/year metadata from Marcoulides (2005) to Larose and Larose (2014), a bibliographic update.

P1.justification: The preprint notice becomes an ICML/PMLR publication notice, a code footnote is added, and the Churn citation and bibliography entry are revised. Scientific prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The enlarged first-page footer changes subsequent column and page breaks, and running headers shift slightly. Figures, tables, captions and appendix graphics retain the same content and display structure.

improvement.justification: The revision updates publication and bibliographic metadata and makes minor layout adjustments. Methods, proofs, empirical support, limitations and reproducibility information remain unchanged, with no meaningful net difference in overall quality.
